projects.title: Dama de la Primavera
projects.description:
My Editor’s Letter

Spring has always been at the heart of life in Antioquia. It has shaped much of our prominence within the floral industry, while its colorful and natural presence has helped define the local artistic vision, remaining a constant force in the cultural identity of our department.

It is no coincidence that we have become known around the world as the “Land of Eternal Spring.” Here, spring is more than a season; it is a fundamental part of our identity and holds a special place in the heart of every paisa.

With this in mind, debuting our “Ladies of the Seasons” series with spring represented a risk for the entire Angelo Studio team.

“Ladies of the Seasons” is our way of interpreting the culture, art, and fashion of each season through the image and perspective of local individuals. Introducing this concept for the first time through a season as symbolic as spring was, if we are being honest, intimidating. We worried that our readers might feel we were altering their perception of the season, or even misinterpreting the culture surrounding it.

Our editorial producer, literary content director, and cover star for this issue, Guadalupe Campuzano Toro, embodies this year’s Lady of Spring perfectly.

It is no secret—especially to those who know me—that Guadalupe has been one of my closest friends for many years. Precisely because of that, I initially hesitated to consider her for the role. At Angelo Studio, we are committed to choosing people who genuinely represent the essence of each concept, without allowing personal relationships to influence our decisions.

Yet the more I searched, the clearer it became: the person I was looking for was, in fact, the very person I had been most reluctant to choose.

Guadalupe was not simply the best option; she had unconsciously become the reference point against which I was measuring everyone else throughout the process. I realized that I did not need to search for someone who fit my vision. I needed to recognize the muse who had already defined it.

Guadalupe hesitated at first. Her reserved and humble nature made her question whether she truly deserved the role. Even so, she chose to take on the challenge.

Both in front of the camera and through her writing, she brought a unique sensitivity to the issue, particularly in her reflection on what it means to be a Lady of Spring. Her commitment to this edition has been absolute, and every contribution she made has been fundamental to the final result.

Although this is only our second edition, it has become one of the most personally significant issues we have created. It demanded more from us, challenged us, and forced us to grow. It is the result of a team learning how to build something with intention.

This is not simply another edition.

It is the beginning of how Angelo Studio intends to define culture moving forward.

— Miguel (Angelo) Gibbs V.
